citations.narrative:
- Multiple juvenile budgie cages had an inadequate amount of perch space for the number of birds contained in those
enclosures. All perching bird species must be provided with proper perches and sufficient space for all individuals to use
the perches at the same time. Lack of perch space can lead to stress and potentially negative health impacts.
Multiple adult cages contained perches that were angled, not level. This forces the birds to perch in an unusual posture
that could negatively impact their welfare over time. Perches should be level or very close to level to protect the well being
of the budgies.
The facility must ensure that all animals have access to an adequate amount of perch space and that only appropriate
perches are used. Perches must be secured in an appropriate orientation to ensure all birds are able to utilize the perches
in a natural manner.

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
- Building 4 had an excessive accumulation of old feed, waste and debris in the front corner under and around stored
equipment. Facility employees had failed to address this area at the most recent cleaning. Accumulation of waste can
have a negative impact on the welfare of the birds in that building, and could also be an attractant to pests and insects.
The facility must clean this area and must ensure that all areas of each building are cleaned on an appropriate schedule.
This is a (1st) Re-License Inspection for a Class “A” license. The inspection and exit briefing were conducted with the
applicant.
All items must be in compliance within 2 more inspections or by 2 September 2026 or the applicant will forfeit the license
fee and must wait 6 months to reapply. Please contact your inspector to schedule your next Re-License Inspection.
Regulated activity can continue under your existing USDA license until it expires.
Additional Inspectors:
CODY YAGER, Avian Field Specialist n
